problem: A school bus accelerates from rest with a constant acceleration of $30\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$ for the first $2$ hours of its motion. It then travels at a constant speed for the next $2$ hours before decelerating with a constant deceleration of $20\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}$ until it stops. Which graph represents the described motion?

feedback.problem: A man accelerates from rest with a constant acceleration of $0.3\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ for the first $10$ seconds of his motion. He then jogs at a constant speed for the next $20$ seconds before accelerating with a constant acceleration of $0.1\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ for another $20$ seconds. Which graph represents the described motion?
feedback.worked_solution:
We start the first line from the point $(0,0),$ since the man starts from rest. Then, because the acceleration is $0.3\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ we draw a line with slope $0.3.$ 

However, because the man is only accelerating for the first $10$ seconds, we stop the line at $t=10.$ At this time, the man's speed has increased by $0.3\cdot 10=3\text{ m/s}.$ So, the first line segment goes from $(0,0)$ to $(10,3).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945962/assets/b458ff6f5f08f548b07923e09aacdc103c8052103736b1adc4a76de120ade097.png)

The man then travels at a constant speed for the next $20$ seconds. So, the speed remains at $3\,\text{m/s}$ for the next $20$ seconds, until $t=10+20=30.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945962/assets/5c6ddd0eb8c72643fa2272f10502e8428d9c30c79d0804c54cfd7347f2178bb8.png)

After $t=30$, the man has an acceleration of $0.1\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ so the slope of the third line segment is $0.1.$ The third line segment stops after $20$ seconds. To figure out the velocity at this moment, we need to find the equation for the third line segment.

Since the third line segment passes through the point $(30,3)$ and has a slope of $0.1,$ we can use point-slope form to write the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}v-{v}_{1} & =m(t-{t}_{1}) \\ v-3 & =0.1(t-30) \\ v-3 & =0.1t-3 \\ v & =0.1t\end{aligned}
$$

The third line segment stops when $t=30+20=50$ seconds, and the velocity at this moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =0.1t \\ v & =0.1(50) \\ v & =5\end{aligned}
$$

So, the third line segment stops at the point $(50,5).$ The final graph is
